parcel.note: The 2010 survey and EAS both give this property as 4702–04 Third Street on parcel 5311026. That parcel has been retired; the assessor now carries the site as 5311039, addressed 4700–4706 Third Street. The assessor dates the building 1900; the 2010 survey dates it about 1885. Most pre-1906 buildings in the district carry a default assessor date of 1900, because the city's building records were destroyed in the 1906 earthquake and fire.

hook: A large Italianate commercial block of about 1885, among the best-preserved Victorian commercial buildings on Third Street.

historic_survey.survey: Bayview-Hunters Point Area B Survey, Town Center Activity Node
historic_survey.cr_status_note: Assigned on architectural criteria alone; the survey records it as provisional pending further research.
historic_survey.rating_note: The survey reports ratings from the 1976 citywide architectural survey on a 0-5 scale, 5 being individual significance of the highest degree. It gives no scale for the Carey & Company or UMB survey ratings, so those are recorded here but not shown on the page.

historical_record.description: Built as a large Italianate commercial block on Railroad Avenue, as Third Street was then named — a store, restaurant or saloon at street level with flats above, chamfered bay windows and a bracketed cornice. It is among the better-preserved Victorian-era commercial buildings in the Town Center, and among the mixed-use buildings on Third Street that survive from the 1899–1900 Sanborn era.
